notes: Paper network: the drawing area grows with the number of papers. Drag to move around, pinch or use +/− to zoom, and the arrow button shows everything again.
Search: new "Coded passages" option searches only what you coded (passage text, your comments and code names), optionally limited to chosen codes.
Copying text from a paper with a spaceless text layer (⌘C) now gives properly spaced text.

Web pages saved as PDF are recognised: the organisation behind the site becomes the author (APA style, e.g. ENTSO-E), the year is the year you saved the page, the site name stands in for the journal, and the address is kept for the reference list.

Export: new "Research dossier" (Markdown) marked as the best choice for Claude and other AI: codebook, every paper with reference and summary, your coded passages in reading order with page, codes and comments, and your notebook.
Export all papers as one ZIP of PDFs, and a share button at the bottom of the left bar opens the export list.
Paper priority: hover a paper in the left bar and click one of three "!" (click the same one again to clear it). Set priorities stay visible, and "Priority" is a new group-by option.

Auto-code per code: hover a code in the right bar and click "Autocode". The AI learns from the passages you coded with it, looks through all papers for similar passages and suggests them. You review and confirm every suggestion; nothing is coded automatically. A warning appears when fewer than 5 passages are coded.
Papers no longer open as tabs (tabs stay for searches and notebook pages). Fixed a crash when coding text inside a framed table.

Memory: Scholia now keeps only a few papers in memory, cleans up after each paper it reads in the background and limits its text caches. If memory ever grows unusually large it saves a short report about what it was doing (Application Support/Scholia/MemoryReports), so the cause can be found and fixed.
Notebook: typing # (or ##, ###) followed by text turns the line into a heading right away, even without a space.
Library: Topics shows whether the AI analysis is up to date, long journal names are readable, and the paper network no longer claims to be up to date when you have added new papers.
Edit info & tags: the Group field can be typed into again and its menu offers “No group” and your groups.
Paper status: right-click a paper to mark it Open, Work in progress (yellow), Done (green) or Ruled out (pale). "Status" is also a grouping option in the left bar.
Quotes with missing spaces: Scholia detects PDFs whose text layer lost its spaces and offers "Fix missing spaces" (re-reads the pages and repairs saved quotes).
Notebook: pictures (paste, drop or /picture) and round bullets.
Coded passages can be lengthened or shortened: select one and drag the handles at its start and end.
Left bar: the project name above the search field is gone; the search field has its full width.
Watchlist: references in PDFs without spaces between words are read correctly (spaces repaired, multi-word surnames like "van der Veen" handled).

Journal page numbers: Scholia finds the real page numbers of papers that are only a page range of an issue (e.g. pp. 917–931) and uses them for quotes, citations, exports and search results. Right-click a paper ▸ Journal page numbers, or use the … menu to detect them for all papers.
Updating no longer leaves two copies of Scholia open: the old one is always closed, and a leftover old copy is closed when the new one starts.

Watchlist “Re-check” is now much more thorough: the AI looks at the actual page pictures (the page where you marked the citation and the last page of the paper) instead of the OCR text, finds the full reference and then looks up the DOI. It costs a few cents more per entry and shows the price first.

Important fix: the AI search could get stuck on some pages and use up all of the Mac's memory. This is fixed, and Scholia now also watches its own memory and saves and closes itself before it could ever slow your Mac down.
A welcome tour for new users that shows around the app and explains what a code is (replay it under Help ▸ Welcome tour).
Confetti when you create your very first code.
Lower AI costs: background tasks no longer spend tokens on long hidden reasoning.
Long code names wrap onto several rows in the labels next to the PDF.
Clearer AI: every analysis view says whether it runs on your Mac or uses AI, and Settings lists where AI is used. The sparkle “Name & tag” button now stays for 30 seconds after an upload.
The Word cloud button next to Auto-code now shows that paper only (computed on your Mac, no AI).

More reliable watchlist: references are looked up in the paper's own reference list (also numbered ones), DOIs come from Crossref and OpenAlex, and a new “Re-check” button reads incomplete entries again in precise mode.
New bug icon in the top bar: report a bug or suggest a feature as a draft on GitHub (nothing is sent automatically).

Paper network: click a circle to see which paper it is (title, authors, how it connects) and open it. In the Library every paper now has the colour of the cluster it sits in, and a ring marks papers that fit more than one topic.
You can now use Mistral instead of Claude: choose the AI provider in Settings (separate key, models and prices for each).
The tour mentions that Scholia is a vibe-coded app, and the Library no longer shuffles papers, authors or journals with equal counts when you click elsewhere.
Notebook: the main page lists its subpages as clickable chapters, renaming a page updates the links to it, the / menu selects the highlighted command with Return, and long gaps after links are gone.

Notebook quotes: “To notebook” copies the quote with its citation and opens the notebook, ready to paste. Quotes from papers are shown as highlighted blocks and are locked against accidental edits (right-click ▸ Edit this quote).

Notebook: /page inserts a link to the new subpage where your cursor was, ⌘⌫ deletes to the start of the line, ⌘Z / ⇧⌘Z undo and redo work reliably, and formatting marks (#, **, *, `) only show on the line or word where your cursor is.

Paper network: a status line says whether AI classification is up to date or how many pairs are still unjudged (with price), and topic-similar pairs the AI has already looked at are never paid for twice. The left bar is now sorted by year by default.
Quality signals in each paper summary (from OpenAlex): peer-reviewed article or preprint, retraction warning, number of citations, journal h-index and first/last author h-index.

Pin papers to the top of the left bar (right-click ▸ Pin to top). New papers without a year, journal or author appear at the top of the list, and papers that were never named keep a one-click “Name & tag” button.
Right-click anywhere on a paper row to get the full menu, including “Name & tag with AI”.
The paper network writes the relation on every line (cites, supports, contradicts, …) and shows clearly which paper cites which, with larger arrows.
Library: every topic cluster now shows its papers, and clicking a journal bar lists the papers published there.
Watchlist: adding a paper that is already in your project (or arrives later) offers to remove it from the watchlist; the Watchlist section in the left bar can be folded away.
Scholia remembers what you had open: project, paper tabs, reading position and notebook tabs are back when you start it again.
The first time an API key is added you choose your standard model yourself, with prices shown.
Top bar reordered: Papers, Notebook, Library, Watchlist, Network, Co-occurrence, Focus, Coffee, Search, Panel. Word cloud and Summary moved next to Auto-code in the paper toolbar.
⌘C now copies text selected in the reader, code labels no longer paint over the toolbar, the ⌘ key-tip popup is gone, and look-alike code colours are separated automatically.
Summaries are read more reliably when the AI answer is slightly malformed.
Paper network shows every paper once: duplicate copies are merged and papers no longer appear to cite themselves
Both graphs (paper network and shared authors) now use gravity: the most connected papers sit in the middle and names no longer overlap

Marking text: all your codes are shown alphabetically over as many rows as needed, with a search field that already has the cursor — type to narrow them, ↩ applies the first match or creates a new code
Shared authors: one small clickable row per paper under each author
Uploading many papers stays smooth, with progress shown; OCR and AI work run a few at a time
After adding several papers: one click to name, tag and summarise them all, with a cost estimate first (also in the Library)
Background AI work (summaries, naming, topics, network, auto-coding) uses Sonnet 5.5 by default, and summaries never start without asking
README with screenshots on GitHub

Search (magnifier in the top bar): find text across all papers, a group or chosen papers, with AND / OR / NOT and "phrases", or ask a question with AI. Results are a clickable list of passages and stay in their own tab until you close it.
Every new code gets a colour clearly different from your existing ones; the palette button in the Codes header spreads look-alike colours apart.

Watchlist: marking an in-text citation now finds the full reference in that paper's reference list (title, authors, journal, DOI). Watched papers show up as dashed placeholders at the top of the left bar, and when the paper lands in your library you are offered to remove it from the watchlist.
Scholia remembers what you had open: when you start it again, your project, paper tabs, reading position in each paper and notebook tabs are back.
Read and annotate PDFs with OCR for scans, highlights and margin code labels
Code passages and figures; AI suggestions and an AI auto-coder you review like tracked changes
Notebook with @ paper tags, citations that jump back to the exact passage, and a reference list
Library overview, word clouds, co-occurrence, AI paper summaries and a paper-relationship network
Your API key stays in your own Keychain; everything else stays on your Mac
